findings.claim: The timeout constant is hard-coded at 10 seconds with no configuration override, which may be too short or too long for some deployments.
findings.test_or_reason: No test or configuration mechanism covers the value; the test only checks it is positive and <= 30000 ms.

findings.claim: The test for R3 mocks AbortSignal.timeout to return an already-aborted signal, which does not exercise the real timeout expiry path (the actual 10-second wait is not tested).
findings.test_or_reason: The test verifies the route handles an aborted signal, but not that the timeout actually fires after the configured duration.

findings.claim: The test double for fetch is more permissive than the real fetch: it does not enforce that the signal is actually used to abort the underlying request, and it does not model the real fetch's behavior of rejecting on abort.
findings.evidence: Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1240-connector-token-security-validate-fetch-is-bounded.test.ts:49-55 `function neverAnswers(init?: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<Response> { ... if (!signal) return; if (signal.aborted) reject(new Error('aborted')); else signal.addEventListener('abort', () => reject(new Error('aborted'))); }`
findings.test_or_reason: The fake only rejects when the signal is aborted; it does not simulate the real fetch's behavior of rejecting with a DOMException or similar when the signal aborts, but the route's catch-all still returns 502.

findings.claim: The test suite does not include a test that verifies the timeout value is actually 10 seconds; it only checks it is positive and <= 30000 ms.
findings.evidence: Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/__tests__/ks1240-connector-token-security-validate-fetch-is-bounded.test.ts:75-83 `it('RED KS-1240 R2 the bound handed to AbortSignal.timeout is positive and at most 30000 ms', ...)`
findings.test_or_reason: The test allows any value between 1 and 30000 ms, so the specific 10-second bound is not pinned.
